column3: NKJV phrases the statement as a question (“Why do …?”), following the Textus Receptus; the critical text is a statement.
Close to the Greek; “the sons of the bridechamber” is rendered “the friends of the bridegroom.”
NKJV has “puts a piece from a new garment,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “having torn a piece from a new garment.”
NKJV includes “and both are preserved,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV has “better” and “immediately,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “The old is good” and lacks “immediately.”
